articles.title: Union Saint-Gilloise - Real Sociedad en directo | Última hora de Europa League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Le han puesto a Oyarzabal al senegalés Sylla, que le sigue a todos lados, ahora cuerpeando de nuevo con él en la línea de fondo, y no le deja ni respi
articles.body:
Última hora del Union Saint-Gilloise - Real Sociedad- Oporto, en directo:

La Real Sociedad tratará de poner hoy fin a la gran racha de 13 partidos sin perder como local del Union Saint-Gilloise, todos los que ha disputado este 2026 y el último del pasado año, y traerse de Bélgica a San Sebastián una victoria que le permita recuperar los punto s, sobre todo, y el optimismo perdidos para esta Europa League tras el 1-2 frente al Bournemouth en Anoeta, en la jornada inaugural. El sueño en esta competición sigue siendo llegar muy lejos.

La Real llega a esta cita en un gran momento, como hemos destacado estos días previos en MARCA, ya que ha vuelto a ser sexta en la clasificación de LaLiga 29 meses después, gracias a los 13 puntos sumados de los últimos 18 , el tercer equipo que más, y lo ha hecho con hasta 10 goleadores diferentes.

Los onces esperados en el USG - Real Sociedad.

Y es que Matarazzo ha conseguido que su equipo saque adelante sus partidos sin depender tanto como antes de las dianas de Mikel Oyarzabal y Take Kubo, aún inéditos este curso, u Orri Óskarsson , el otro gran realizador de la pasada campaña. Los tres, por cierto, apuntan a volver hoy al equipo titular, después de no jugar el primero más que 40 minutos ante el Dépor, una cita en la que el segundo no saltó al césped y que el tercero se perdió por estar sancionado.

Serán algunos de los futbolistas con los que el técnico de Nueva Jersey tiene pinta que va a refrescar su once inicial. Marrero en la portería, Fort y Zubeldia en la defensa, Gorrotxategi y Turrientes en el centro del campo y Kubo en el ataque pueden ser otras de las caras nuevas. Sería una sorpresa que muchos de estos hombres no tuvieran hoy la oportunidad de demostrar que pueden seguir siendo considerados como titulares, pese a que últimamente les esté tocando ser más suplentes.

La idea de la Real será ser el primer equipo en vencer a domicilio a su rival de esta tarde en este 2026, después de que 13 no lo hayan podido hacer, entre ellos el Atalanta y el Bodo Glimt en la Champions, y el Anderlecht, el Brujas o el Genk , en el campeonato belga, en el que aún no ha caído en este curso.

Por si fuera poco, el Union Saint-Gilloise se estrenó en esta fase Liga de la Europa League con un contundente 0-3 en la visita a un viejo conocido de la Real, el Viktoria Plzen , por lo que superarle sería privar que uno de los líderes hiciera pleno y empezar a situarse en la parte media de la clasificación, sin perder de vista los ocho primeros puestos que llevan directamente a los octavos.

La Real estará arropado por unos 550 seguidores , a los que el club txuriurdin ha enviado sus localidades a través del correo electrónico. El de encuentro de todos ellos será Oude Markt, una plaza situada en el centro de la ciudad, con varios bares y restaurantes. Las 14.00 horas es a la que se pide a la afición realista que haga acto de presencia, para ir desde ese lugar al campo, un recorrido de sólo 15 minutos, recordando la prohibición de consumir bebidas alcohólicas en la calle. La grada destinada a la afición visitante se encuentra ubicada en la puerta 'Away Entrance - Tervuursevest' y el deseo es abandonarla unas horas más tarde tras disfrutar de un triunfo.

articles.title: El Athletic lucirá un tercer patrocinador en la camiseta
articles.standfirst: El club rojiblanco anuncia que renueva el acuerdo comercial con Vueling hasta 2030
articles.summary: El club rojiblanco anuncia que renueva el acuerdo comercial con Vueling hasta 2030
articles.body: El Athletic estrenará camiseta frente al Valencia. El club incorporará desde sábado a Vueling como patrocinador de su camiseta. El logo de la aerolínea, que hasta ahora figuraba en el pantalón, aparecerá en la manga izquierda de la camiseta, que dando reservada la derecha para el logo de la competición en juego. El patrocinador central seguirá siendo Kutxabank mientras que en la trasera aparece Digi. Vueling, que seguirá en los pantalones de entrenamiento, ha renovado el convenio de colaboración por cuatro temporadas. El club se asegura un patrocinador catalogado como premium por la entidad. Además, en las próximas semanas la aerolínea mostrará el nuevo diseño del avión personalizado con imagenes rojiblancas, que Vueling utiliza en vuelos regulares. Según detalla el club en un comunicado, "la renovación da continuidad a ocho años de colaboración y estará acompañada por la campaña Arrimar el hombro, que pone el acento en el apoyo mutuo, el sentimiento de pertenencia y el trabajo en equipo. La relación entre ambas entidades consolida a Vueling como un aliado clave para la movilidad y la proyección internacional de la entidad rojiblanca, con la que colabora estrechamente desde 2018".

articles.title: Gulacsi vuelve a los entrenamientos tras su “profundamente traumática” experiencia
articles.standfirst: El guardameta se ha reincorporado hoy al trabajo tras sufrir un asalto a mano armada en su domicilio
articles.summary: El guardameta se ha reincorporado hoy al trabajo tras sufrir un asalto a mano armada en su domicilio
articles.body: Tras vivir una experiencia “profundamente traumática” en palabras del propio afectado, el portero del Villarreal, Peter Gulacsi ,se reincorporó este jueves a los entrenamientos junto al resto de sus compañeros. De esta forma, el guardameta húngaro vuelve al equipo después de haber sido baja el pasado martes en el partido ante el Nápoles tras ser víctima, junto a su familia, de un asalto nocturno a mano armada en su propio domicilio. El chalet del futbolista, ubicado en una urbanización de la localidad valenciana de Puzol, fue asaltado por varios atracadores en la madrugada del lunes mientras el jugador y su familia dormían. Tras amenazarlos con un arma, y después de ser retenidos durante casi una hora, se llevaron un botín en el que costaban bolsos y relojes de lujo. El impacto emocional impidió al jugador disputar el partido del pasado martes. Este jueves se sumó al trabajo junto al resto del equipo y se espera que forme parte de la convocatoria que el sábado se medirá al Elche. El experimentado cancerbero, que está firmando una muy buena temporada en el conjunto castellonense, lanzó un mensaje de agradecimiento en sus redes sociales y pidió respeto a su privacidad: “Muchas gracias por todos sus mensajes, amabilidad y apoyo. Realmente lo apreciamos. Los eventos del lunes por la noche fueron profundamente traumáticos, tener nuestro hogar y el sentido de seguridad violados es algo que llevará tiempo procesar, pero sobre todo, estamos agradecidos de que nuestra familia esté a salvo. Ahora nos gustaría dejar esta experiencia atrás, tanto como sea posible, volver a nuestra vida cotidiana y pedir amablemente a todos que respeten nuestra privacidad y nos permitan avanzar”

articles.title: Tom Shaw: Lincoln City will not be defined by 6-0 West Ham defeat
articles.summary: Lincoln City will not be defined by their 6-0 Championship defeat by West Ham, says Imps head coach Tom Shaw.
articles.body:
Hit for six when two men down, Lincoln City were outplayed and outgunned by West Ham on a night that head coach Tom Shaw described as a "brutal experience" for the Imps.

And yet Shaw, who shares his role as Lincoln boss with Chris Cohen, defiantly says they will not be defined by the horror defeat inflicted on them by a Hammers side who were playing Premier League football just five months ago.

Two red cards in the opening 23 minutes, with Tom Hamer's dismissal after 160 seconds followed by Conor McGrandles' sending-off, had Lincoln – a club with one of the smallest budgets in the Championship – facing what Shaw called an "impossible situation" against the favourites for promotion.

It took until the 45th minute for Konstantinos Mavropanos to break the deadlock, but a five-goal avalanche followed after the break with substitute Edvin Austbo, Jarrod Bowen and Pablo netting before fit-again Czech Republic international Tomas Soucek came off the bench to complete the 6-0 win with a late double.

"In a weird way I think our boys will come out a little bit stronger from going to the dark moments and the dark place they've had to when being two men down against that quality," Shaw told BBC Sport.

"In the unique situation, I don't think it affects stuff and it won't define anything."

West Ham were the first of the teams relegated from the Premier League last season to face Lincoln, a club back in the second tier for the first time after a 65-year absence.

With the Hammers having won the Europa Conference League by beating Italian side Fiorentina a little over three years earlier, their trip to the 11,000-capacity ProAmpac Stadium was seen as a "monster fixture" for Lincoln, a club who were playing non-league football less than a decade ago.

And it is more than just a couple of divisions that have separated these two sides in years gone by.

West Ham, whose 62,500-seat London Stadium home was built and used for the 2012 Olympic Games, took a squad that cost more than £200m to Lincolnshire on Wednesday.

Starting for the Hammers was Max Kilman, whose £40m transfer from Wolves to West Ham in 2024 cost more than four times the total amount Lincoln have paid for players in their 142-year existence.

When asked if the heavy defeat delivered by the Hammers, and the financial gulf between the two clubs, underlined how much of an "underdog" Lincoln are on their return to the second tier, Shaw replied by saying it was a tag they were eager to shake off – even if it is a fitting label.

"The outside world perhaps label it as that at times, but we don't want to be that any more. We don't want to feel like that any more," he said.

"We want to take the game to some of these teams and that is our intention.

"We've had some really good results and we've competed in the majority of these games. So we've got to grow now. We've got to grow as a team, as a staff, as a football club. We've got to grow into the Championship properly and people can label us as the underdogs, but we won't be playing like it."

West Ham score six in rout of nine-man Lincoln

Lincoln City 0-6 West Ham United - fans' verdicts

The defeat was Lincoln's heaviest of the season and extended their losing run to three matches.

Before that, however, back-to-back victories on the road at Preston North End and Bristol City had the Imps in eighth spot.

Shaw, who defended both Hamer and McGrandles by saying "they'll never let us down" despite each being shown a straight red card, lamented that his side "didn't get a proper game" against the Hammers.

"We go away thinking we could have had a good old ding-dong with them, but once the red cards happen it's a very, very tough situation," Shaw said.

articles.title: Vinicius Junior: From contract uncertainty to conspiracy theories and a four-match ban
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr speaks to the press after being handed a four-match ban following his red card against Villarreal.
articles.body:
A bizarre online rumour, a red card and a four-match suspension have put Vinicius Jr back into the spotlight at a crucial point in Real Madrid's season.

First, over the summer, came the uncertainty over his future at Real Madrid, with contract talks stalling for more than 18 months and Arsenal reportedly among the clubs interested in the Brazilian.

Those negotiations eventually reached a resolution, with Vinicius securing an improved deal, but the headlines have continued.

Then came bizarre conspiracy theories claiming he had been replaced by a body double, following cosmetic surgery he had done after the World Cup.

Now, following his dismissal against Villarreal at the weekend, a four-match suspension means he is ruled out of El Clasico against Barcelona a week on Sunday.

But beyond the social media frenzy and disciplinary controversy, bigger questions are emerging about Vinicius' form, his on-pitch behaviour and his relationship with the Real Madrid supporters.

A key moment was when Jose Mourinho opted to start the Brazilian on the bench for the match against Villarreal, their first since the international break.

It was the first time since last April that Vinicius had not started a match for the club, with Mourinho handing Yan Diomande a place in the starting XI instead.

"What makes me sad is the fact he really wants to be at his absolute best," Mourinho said beforehand.

"He wants to be the Vini who wins games, scores goals and makes the difference. Seeing the pain he feels himself makes me sad. He is an extraordinary guy who works very hard to get back to his absolute best.

"He deserves better treatment, as he has made Madrid very happy on many occasions."

Vinicius has been continually booed and whistled by some Real Madrid supporters this season, along with other players.

After entering the game in the 52nd minute he looked to have made an immediate impact, scoring what Real believed to be their second goal after a Jude Bellingham assist.

Vinicius raced towards the supporters, kissing the badge before being engulfed by his team-mates, who piled on top of him in celebration.

Even Mourinho sprinted across the pitch to join the celebrations, which felt like a public display of his faith in the Brazilian.

The referee was sent to the monitor, which showed Vinicius pulling Nathan Saliba's hair while the ball was in play and neither player was challenging for it.

The referee overturned the goal and instead showed Vinicius a straight red card.

The Brazilian's reaction to the decision then became a further disciplinary issue, with team-mates having to intervene as he continued to protest.

Mourinho refused to speak to press afterwards. News travelled around the media room that Mourinho felt if he did speak, he would say something that would get him suspended.

Two hours before Real faced Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee handed Vinicius a four-match suspension.

Two matches were imposed for the hair-pulling incident, with a further two for his protests following the dismissal.

The punishment rules him out of league fixtures against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Most significantly, it means he will miss El Clasico, unless an appeal changes the outcome.

Mourinho expressed his frustration at the timing of the announcement, questioning why it came just two hours before their Champions League match.

"Do you think it's normal for a player who is going to play an important match for Spanish football to know two hours before that he is sanctioned with four games? You don't need to answer me," Mourinho said.

"It's not normal. Couldn't they do it now or tomorrow morning? We found out on the bus and almost arrived at the stadium."

The Portuguese coach described the decision as showing "little respect" for the club and suggested the timing was intentional, particularly with Madrid facing a demanding schedule in the coming days.

Following Real Madrid's 4-3 victory over Roma, Vinicius also addressed the incident, having apologised to his team and fans on social media.

"I don't remember any player ever getting a four-game suspension," Vinicius said. "I tried to get past the player in front of me and ended up grabbing his hair.

"That's it – a red card. That's why I was so surprised, but I didn't say a single bad word to the referee to deserve a four-game suspension."

The forward also acknowledged his frustration at being substituted in the 59th minute against Roma when Real Madrid were trailing 3-1. They then scored three late goals to stage a remarkable comeback win.

"It's normal for me to get upset after being substituted because I always want to play every match," he said.

"I'm aware of my form and how I'm playing. I'm here to help the team, and sometimes I need to come off so other players can play and change the dynamics."

The Brazilian has gone six appearances for Real Madrid without scoring, with his last goal coming in August against Real Sociedad.

The 26-year-old has also become the subject of bizarre conspiracy theories on social media after undergoing a cosmetic surgery procedure on his chin in July.

Because of the visible differences, rumours on social media suggested Vinicius had been replaced by a body double.

Meanwhile, Vinícius's personal life has also made headlines in Brazil, with his reported split from Brazilian-American television personality Virginia Fonseca dominating coverage over the weekend.

The internet may continue searching for extraordinary explanations on why Vinicius has experienced a dip in form, but Real Madrid need to find answers on the pitch.

The win against Roma, especially coming from two goals down, was described by Vinicius as a "huge boost for the team".

He assured fans that he will be back to his best form as soon as possible.

"I know I'm not at my best right now, but I've had worse moments, and even when people doubted me, I've always stood up for this club," he said.

"That's why I renewed for six more years. The good streak will return, and the goals will come back. I'm sure of that. I have no doubt. I'm here to help the team."

articles.title: French football body urges fans and students to keep politics out of stadiums
articles.summary: French Football Federation’s ethics body calls for neutrality amid student protests.
articles.body:
The ethics body of the French football federation is urging fans to stay neutral amid the nationwide student protests that are drawing international attention.

The police response to the largely peaceful demonstrations has prompted widespread accusations of brutality, and football fans in stadiums have expressed their support for students.

Officers have made extensive use of tear gas and batons to disperse crowds. More than 6,600 arrests were made nationwide as of last week, an unusually high number for a French protest movement.

A police tear gas grenade shattered a 14-year-old’s jaw and many of his teeth, while a 15-year-old lost a hand in an incident involving a stun grenade. Other teenagers have also suffered life-changing injuries blamed on police weaponry during protests.

During a Ligue 1 match between Lens and Lyon last week, the home fans unfurled a banner calling for an end to the “disproportionate and systematic police violence,” according to the National Council for Football Ethics (CNE).

The CNE also noted that at the half-hour mark of the match between PSG and Le Mans, supporters displayed a banner reading: “Your militias repress; our youth resists.”

The ethics body said in a statement that it was easy to understand why young supporters, who are often students, might take advantage of matches to publicly express their support for the demonstrators.

However, it added that the principle of political neutrality is “enshrined” in the laws of sport, both internationally through the Olympic Charter and FIFA statutes, and at a national level.

The CNE recalled that any speech or display of a political, ideological, religious or trade union nature are prohibited, as is the wearing of symbols or clothing that expresses political, philosophical, religious or trade union affiliation.

“Sport should unite, not divide,” it said. “The National Council for Football Ethics therefore calls on all supporters, who are an integral part of the football family, to uphold the principle of neutrality in all circumstances.

“The aim is to ensure that the stadium does not become a political or trade union battleground, but remains a place of celebration and shared enjoyment centred on sport.”

articles.title: Trump's intervention in Folarin Balogun red card prompts FIFA to revisit suspension rules: reports

articles.body: It has been four months since Folarin Balogun's suspension from a red card was lifted in controversial fashion, and its effects remain ongoing. In the United States Men's National Team's Round of 32 World Cup match against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Balogun, the USMNT's best player in the tournament at that point, was given a questionable red card, automatically suspending him for the next game against Belgium. articles.title: Eom Jisung: Swansea winger has strength to move on after alleged racial abuse
articles.summary: Vitor Matos says Eom Jisung has the strength to move on from the alleged racial abuse which marred Swansea City's win at Millwall.
articles.body:
Vitor Matos says Eom Jisung has the strength to move on from the alleged racial abuse which marred Swansea City's win at Millwall.

The Metropolitan Police is investigating after Swansea's staff reported alleged abuse aimed at South Korea international Eom at The Den on Tuesday.

Matos says winger Eom, 24, "feels supported" at Swansea on the back of an incident that is "sad for everyone, either in football or in society".

"You have a behaviour that unfortunately nowadays still happens in the world we live in," the Swansea head coach said.

"We have a tool to fight against that. We used that [by reporting the allegation]; now he's moving on.

"As an adult, he understands that he needs to speak about these situations. You complain about the situation, and you have the strength as well to move on - that's how we should handle it."

Matos reiterated that officials at Millwall "did really well to follow the protocol" after the alleged abuse was reported in the second half of Swansea's 1-0 win, prompting a delay of around seven minutes before the game resumed.

When asked what he expects to come next, Matos added: "That all ways of investigating what happened come to a conclusion and then with that conclusion, hopefully everyone can be aware of that, and Millwall decide to do what they need to do in this kind of situation."

The incident at Millwall came just over a fortnight after it emerged that the Football Association of Ireland was investigating whether Swansea forward Adam Idah was racially abused by Israel supporters during a Nations League fixture with the Republic of Ireland last month.

Matos has spoken to Idah, 25, about what occurred during a match played in Serbia.

"It's a different situation because in the end the referee [in that game] said he didn't hear anything so they could not stop the game," Matos said.

"I was not there, so it's hard for me to judge the situation.

"I was there [at Millwall], I was quite clear the fourth [official] followed the protocol, which I think is the right thing to do in these situations, and now there's an investigation."

Eom, an unused substitute at Millwall, has been in fine form for Swansea this season, while he also helped South Korea win the Asian Games earlier this month.

He will be in contention to feature when Swansea, who are top of the Championship, host third-placed West Ham United on Saturday (15:00 BST).

articles.title: Javier Aguirre acaba con 103 años de tradición en Mestalla
articles.standfirst: El técnico mexicano cambia la ubicación del banquillo del Valencia en la última temporada del coliseo blanquinegro
articles.summary: El técnico mexicano cambia la ubicación del banquillo del Valencia en la última temporada del coliseo blanquinegro
articles.body: El entrenador del Valencia, Javier Aguirre, ha decidido alterar una de las costumbres más arraigadas que recuerdan los más veteranos asiduos a Mestalla. El técnico del Valencia ha ordenado que el equipo local abandone el banquillo que siempre ha ocupado en el lado izquierdo mirando desde la Tribuna para instalarse en el lado opuesto, una medida que estrenará este fin de semana, contra el Athletic, y que rompe con una tradición que se ha mantenido intacta durante décadas. La decisión, adelantada por Tribuna Deportiva, no responde a cuestiones de capacidad ni de comodidad. Ambos banquillos cuentan con las mismas dimensiones y número de asientos, por lo que el cambio tiene más que ver con las preferencias personales del entrenador que con una ventaja funcional. Aguirre ya había impulsado una medida idéntica durante su etapa en el Mallorca, en Son Moix, y ahora ha querido repetir la experiencia en Mestalla. Si hay alguna razón para que el equipo local ocupe ese banquillo desde que se tiene memoria es la cercanía con el vestuario local y que está en el lado izquierdo del pasillo en dirección al césped lo que permite una salida natural de futbolistas, técnicos y staff sin tener que cruzarse con el personal del equipo contrario. La medida adquiere una dimensión especial por el momento en que se produce. El Valencia afronta la recta final en el actual Mestalla desde que se inauguró en 1923 y cada partido está cargado de simbolismo, aunque ahora mismo el equipo esté más inmerso en salir de la crisis deportiva que de evocar la nostalgia. Como cuestión operativa o de funcionamiento, ahora el banquillo local estará más cerca del árbitro asistente que ocupa esa banda durante los partidos. El precedente más parecido se produjo recientemente en el Sevilla, cuando Luis García Plaza solicitó un cambio similar nada más aterrizar en un equipo que atravesaba una etapa compleja, en el Sánchez Pizjuán. En idéntico escenario años atrás, Víctor Espárrago también promovió una modificación de este tipo, aunque posteriormente Carlos Bilardo fin a esa ubicación a la temporada siguiente.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council for his World Cup sell-off plan; FIFA president was speaking in Zurich on Thursday morning; The FA is among European leaders who still want him to resign, while UEFA have called on Infantino to release documents related to the scheme
articles.body:
His expression of regret for not telling the council about his plans earlier was not good enough for European football leaders, including FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who still want him to resign.

UEFA wants Infantino to release all documents relating to the plan as they believe the 20 per cent stake in all future FIFA tournaments was being sold for a knockdown price.

It was expected council members would also quiz Infantino on a number of controversial issues at the meeting.

As well as the World Cup sell-off plan, Infantino faced scrutiny on the decision to suspend the one-match ban of USA striker Folarin Balogun during the World Cup, the FIFA Peace Prize and why it was given to USA President Donald Trump, and the reasons for an additional £1.3m fee he received in 2024 on top of his FIFA salary .

After this summer's World Cup, Infantino abandoned a controversial plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private equity investors after fierce opposition from football's governing bodies.

FIFA had announced it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments.

Infantino had then given football associations until September 19 to back his proposals to sell off part of FIFA to private investors with a £30.1m incentive to accept.

But the controversial proposals received fierce criticism from UEFA, CONCACAF (the North American, Central American and Caribbean association) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

Infantino 'not fit to be FIFA president' if he avoids questions

FA chair Hewitt has called on Infantino to answer questions about his World Cup private investor plan and the Folarin Balogun case.

She said Council members had not received answers to "anything we had specifically requested" regarding FFE or the Balogun incident, where the United States striker's one-match ban was suspended following a call to Infantino from US President Donald Trump.

Hewitt told reporters in Zurich: "The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting.

"He's told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it's up to him to do that, and do that in the open way."

Saying sorry 'not enough for European football leaders'

Analysis by Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"It's not enough for European football leaders, because make no mistake, they have had enough of Gianni Infantino, they want him out.

"They just think this is the final scandal in a long list of scandals - and don't forget what Infantino was doing this summer behind the backs of the FIFA Council, who are effectively the FIFA Board.

"He was negotiating to sell a stake, not just in the World Cup, but all future FIFA tournaments forever more. A 20 per cent stake, he was going to set up a new company, and the company was valued at just $20bn (£15m) when the World Cup this summer made $15bn (£11bn).

"So, European football leaders are convinced he was trying to sell off the World Cup on the cheap. They have gone to the courts to try and force him to release all documents about this plan he had come up with. They are saying today [Thursday], including the chair of the FA, Debbie Hewitt, that basically sorry is not good enough, we need to see the documents, we want to see all the figures, you've got to be transparent, you've got to release all these documents.

"And I think the reason they are so desperate to get their hands on those documents is because they know it will be a massive scandal if they have the evidence to prove the FIFA president was selling off a stake in FIFA tournaments to people with close ties to President Trump for a knockdown price. That would be a big, big story."

Wenger and Figo among potential Infantino rivals for presidency

UEFA still want to put forward a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency.

Infantino is hoping to be re-elected for a fourth term next year, without facing a challenger for the third election a row.

UEFA want him to resign after he became embroiled in a long list of controversies and scandals, but Infantino believes he still has enough support from around the world to win again at the election in Morocco in March.

Arsene Wenger, Luis Figo and Michelle Kang have been mentioned as potential candidates but it remains to be seen whether any of them are prepared to challenge Infantino.

Anyone who wants to take on Infantino has until 18 November to declare their candidacy.

It may be in the best interests of challengers to declare their intention to stand as late as possible in order to give Infantino and his supporters less time to prepare for taking on a rival.

Former Arsenal manager Wenger is respected around the world but he has shown no interest so far in leading FIFA.

He has been happy working as FIFA's global football development chief since 2019, although he did release a statement in August criticising Infantino's plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup. He was appointed to his role by Infantino and has supported some of the FIFA president's most controversial projects, such as a biennial World Cup and an expanded Club World Cup.

Luis Figo has launched a scathing attack on Infantino in a newspaper column, calling for his resignation in the wake of the World Cup sell-off scandal. The former Real Madrid and Barcelona star has the profile to pose a challenge, but his role as a UEFA adviser since 2017 could make it harder to secure the votes he would need from football associations around the world to replace Infantino.

Lyon, London City Lionesses and Washington Spirit owner Kang has also been mentioned as a potential challenger but there have been no indications that she is preparing to take on Infantino.

The FIFA Council has 37 members made up of:

Eight vice presidents including UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and the presidents of the other five confederations. FA chair Debbie Hewitt is also a vice president

28 other members elected by the FIFA member associations

articles.title: Mikey Moore's Germany loan move inspired by Sancho and Bellingham
articles.summary: Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore says the success of Jadon Sancho and Jude Bellingham in the Bundesliga influenced his decision to join Cologne.
articles.body:
Tottenham's Mikey Moore says the success of Jadon Sancho and Jude Bellingham in the Bundesliga influenced his decision to join Cologne on loan.

The 19-year-old became the latest English talent to move to the German top flight after completing a season-long loan move to the RheinEnergieStadion last month.

Moore's move came almost a decade after a 17-year-old Sancho left Manchester City to join Borussia Dortmund.

During his time in Germany, Sancho established himself as one of Europe's most exciting wingers, making more than 150 appearances for Dortmund and helping the club win the DFB-Pokal in 2021. He subsequently secured a £73m move to Manchester United.

Bellingham followed a similar path in 2020, leaving boyhood club Birmingham City to join Dortmund. The midfielder quickly developed into one of the most sought-after players in world football before joining Real Madrid for an initial £88.5m in 2023.

Speaking on Thursday's Euro Leagues podcast - which will be broadcast on BBC Radio 5 Live at 21:00 BST - before Friday's Bundesliga match with Eintracht Frankfurt, Moore revealed that the success of his fellow Englishmen had inspired him to turn down offers from England in favour of a move to Germany.

"I think over the years you've seen so many young players come out here, and there are some really good examples of world-class players like Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho doing really well," Moore said.

"It's a really attractive place to play football, especially for a young attacker. It's a great platform to play, and that was sold to me by the people at the club and the manager.

"They've put real trust in me, and the amount of game time I've played so quickly in my Koln [Cologne] career has been nice. It's been good to have that trust from all the staff and people at the club.

"I'm already happy with my decision. Now I can really kick on, make my own story and build my own path in German football."

'I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone'

Although Moore only turned 19 in August, he is no stranger to stepping outside his comfort zone.

Last season, he made 47 appearances in all competitions, including the Champions League qualifying rounds, during a loan spell at Scottish Premiership side Rangers.

It was the first time Moore had left his boyhood club Tottenham, and he rose to the challenge, scoring six goals and providing two assists in 28 Scottish Premiership appearances.

The experience offered a different test to the one he now faces in Germany, but it provided valuable exposure to the demands of first-team football.

"I had options to stay in England and maybe stay somewhere a little more comfortable," Moore said.

"But the conversations came down to me picking a team, and I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone to test myself in a big league and one of the top five leagues.

"When we were speaking, everyone said they thought it would be a really good experience for me to experience this type of football.

"It's really intense, and there are some great teams in the league.

"For me, it was a no-brainer. I made the decision early that I wanted to come out here, and now I just need to push on."

'I'll try my best to get my hands on Harry Kane's shirt'

It has been a whirlwind few weeks for Moore since moving to Cologne on transfer deadline day.

Having now found an apartment close to fellow England youth internationals Reigan Heskey and Jahmai Simpson-Pusey, who are also on loan at the club, the 19-year-old has turned his attention to learning German.

Moore had his first lesson this week and, at his mother's request, is hoping to expand his vocabulary in the language over the coming weeks.

"I wasn't the brightest at school, so I might take a while to learn the language," Moore joked. "But I think the more hours I put in, I'll pick it up at some point anyway.

"At least I'll be able to learn a few words so I can order my food or something in German."

Fortunately for the attacker, he will not have to rely solely on his German when Cologne travel to face Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich next month.

The fixture will also give him the chance to reunite with Harry Kane, who was still at Tottenham when Moore was first invited to train with the senior squad during the 2021-22 season.

"He's been a massive idol of mine since I was really young. When I first went up to train with the first team under Antonio Conte, Harry Kane was over there, and I'd seen some finishing that I'd never seen anything like again," Moore recalled.

"It will be a great experience to play against him and share a pitch with him. I'm really looking forward to it."

Almost a decade after Sancho's move to the Bundesliga, it is Kane now flying the flag for England in Germany's top flight. Moore, meanwhile, is hoping to leave the Allianz Arena with a special memento of his own.

"I'll try my best to get my hands on that shirt," Moore said. "I saw him on the last international break, actually, and went and said hello. If I see him on the next one, if we're in the same place, I'm definitely going to say to him, 'Give me that shirt when we next play.'

"Hopefully, I'll be coming back to Koln with that in my hand."

articles.title: Luis de la Fuente, doctor 'honoris causa' de la UCAM
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador nacional destaca en el acto que el fútbol "no me ha enseñado únicamente a ganar, me ha enseñado a vivir"
articles.summary: El seleccionador nacional destaca en el acto que el fútbol "no me ha enseñado únicamente a ganar, me ha enseñado a vivir"
articles.body: Con un Templo del Monasterio de Los Jerónimos repleto y ante un prolongado y emocionante aplauso, Luis de la Fuente, seleccionador nacional flamante campeón del mundo, fue investido Doctor Honoris Causa por la UCAM, institución que conmemora el 30 aniversario de su fundación. El acto académico estuvo presidido por María Dolores García, presidenta de la UCAM, acompañada por Josefina García Lozano, rectora de la institución; Fernando López Miras, presidente de la Comunidad Autónoma de la Región de Murcia y José Manuel Lorca Planes, obispo de la diócesis de Cartagena, así como por Rebeca Pérez, alcaldesa de Murcia y Visitación Martínez, presidenta de la Asamblea Regional de Murcia. Lourdes Meroño, decana de la Facultad de Deporte, en la Laudatio ha definido la trayectoria de Luis de la Fuente como “ejemplar”, asegurando que su legado va más allá de los impresionantes títulos que ha logrado, y es el de su capacidad de inspirar a los demás"; en tanto que Alejandro Blanco, presidente del Comité Olímpico Español, hizo hincapié en el gran trabajo desarrollado por De la Fuente a lo largo de toda su carrera y los valores que defiende. Tras asegurar que el seleccionador nacional es un ejemplo de que “también se genera conocimiento fuera del aula”, precisó que es justo merecedor de esta distinción y, además, “representa el trabajo de los miles de entrenadores que están en todos los campos de fútbol en España enseñando a los jóvenes a formarse en este deporte y como personas”. Uno de los momentos más emotivos de la ceremonia ha sido cuando el seleccionador nacional de fútbol recibió los atributos como Doctor Honoris Causa por la Católica (medalla, guantes blancos, anillo y birrete) y, muy especialmente cuando, a instancias de la presidenta de la Universidad, juró su nombramiento y compromiso con la UCAM, lo que provocó el cerrado aplauso del claustro de doctores, directivos de la universidad, alumnos e invitados. Luis de la Fuente, en su Discurso de Investidura titulado ‘Los valores del fútbol como escuela de vida’, destacó que, después de tantos años en el fútbol, “si alguien me preguntara cuál es la enseñanza más importante que me ha dejado este deporte, mi respuesta sería sencilla: no me ha enseñado únicamente a ganar, me ha enseñado a vivir. Y creo que esa es la grandeza del deporte, siendo una de las herramientas educativas más poderosas que existen”. La formación y los valores fueron el eje de su intervención, asegurando que “los mejores vestuarios no eran necesariamente los que tenían más talento; eran los que tenían más valores. Hablo de respeto, de generosidad, de humildad y compromiso” y “las mejores organizaciones, instituciones y comunidades se construyen sobre esos mismos principios”. Para concluir que el deporte tiene una capacidad extraordinaria para ofrecer esos valores “a través de cada entrenador, profesor, investigador, dirigente y deportista. Todos somos modelos para alguien”. El seleccionador nacional transmitió siempre a los futbolistas que ha dirigido la importancia del trabajo en conjunto, porque “el éxito individual merece reconocimiento. El colectivo, en cambio, tiene la capacidad de transformar comunidades enteras. Un equipo funciona cuando cada uno de los miembros que lo conforman entiende que existe algo más importante que ellos mismos”. Y ha añadido que “hay grupos que funcionan como equipos. Y otros que llegan a convertirse en algo mucho más profundo: una familia” para afirmar que “creo que la Selección es un ejemplo de ello”. Además de por sus valores, Luis de la Fuente está vinculado a la UCAM por sus creencias, ya que se ha declarado públicamente a lo largo de los años como católico: “Para mí, todo lo que esté relacionado con la fe supone un motor en la vida y algo muy importante”, afirmó. El 13 de noviembre de 2026 la Universidad Católica de Murcia cumple 30 años. Desde su fundación, José Luis Mendoza impulsó un modelo inspirado en las universidades anglosajonas que integra formación académica, investigación, competición de alto nivel y transmisión de valores. Uno de sus pilares es la alianza con el Comité Olímpico Español, iniciada en 2012 por Mendoza y Alejandro Blanco. Mediante becas, tutorización personalizada y adaptación académica, permite a cientos de deportistas de élite compatibilizar su carrera deportiva con los estudios, y ha hecho de la UCAM un referente internacional en carrera dual. Los resultados olímpicos y paralímpicos reflejan la dimensión de esta apuesta. En Río 2016, los deportistas vinculados a la UCAM lograron 15 medallas y 9 diplomas olímpicos, además de 9 medallas y 3 diplomas paralímpicos. En Tokio 2020, el balance fue de 23 medallistas y 31 diplomas olímpicos y paralímpicos, y en París 2024, de 15 medallistas y 33 deportistas con diploma. Más allá del podio, destaca la formación académica de los deportistas UCAM. Entre los doctores figuran los atletas Juanma Molina y Antonio Peñalver, en Ciencias del Deporte, y el campeón olímpico de taekwondo Joel González, en Criminología. Entre los graduados están Lola Riera, en Medicina, Miguel Ángel López en Ciencias de la Actividad Física y el Deporte, y Artemi Gavezou, en Administración y Dirección de Empresas.

articles.title: FIFA President Infantino apologises to council but critics remain unhappy
articles.summary: FIFA council meeting lasts over three hours as President Gianni Infantino apologises to members, but critics want more.
articles.body:
Gianni Infantino apologised to his toughest critics but provided no new details or documents on FIFA issues that most concern them at a showdown meeting of its ruling council on Thursday.

No documents about the $4.2bn World Cup sell-off plan he launched and dropped in July . No details about the Folarin Balogun red-card case at the World Cup and how US President Donald Trump intervened to help the national team forward.

World football’s ruling body FIFA will, however, review whether to continue awarding the peace prize that was created to be given to Trump in December.

Pressed by European football officials for written evidence about his secretive private equity plan for the World Cup that provoked a global rift, Infantino asked them to submit written questions, FIFA Vice President Debbie Hewitt said after the three-and-a-half-hour meeting .

“The man has to answer those questions. If he doesn’t answer those questions, no, he is not fit to be the FIFA president,” said Hewitt, who leads the English Football Association.

European football’s ruling body UEFA is leading attempts to remove Infantino before or at the FIFA presidential election in March and heard little to change that view Thursday.

“No satisfactory answers were provided,” said German football chief Bernd Neuendorf, one of eight UEFA delegates in the 37-member FIFA Council that Infantino chairs. It had not met since Infantino provoked the crisis.

“We need a person of integrity, someone who can be expected to restore the reputation of the association, which has undoubtedly been lost,” Neuendorf told reporters.

Infantino did start the meeting by apologising to his council colleagues for blindsiding them and creating a furore over his private investor plan with venture capitalist Joshua Kushner that was revealed in media reports nine days after the World Cup final in July.

“He said that with some contrition,” Hewitt said.

UEFA also has asked courts in the United States for the right to get evidence for a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland. The court filings allege possible mismanagement of FIFA finances in the value he put on the intended subsidiary running tournament commercial rights.

It was to be at least 20 percent owned by investors led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner.

articles.title: El Granada despega en la carretera y puede volar en Los Cármenes
articles.standfirst: Los de Pacheta, el tercer mejor visitante de la categoría, afrontan cuatro de las próximas cinco jornadas en su feudo
articles.summary: Los de Pacheta, el tercer mejor visitante de la categoría, afronta cuatro de las próximas cinco jornadas en su feudo
articles.body: El Granada tenía un inicio de competición muy exigente, con rivales de primer nivel y, además, seis partidos lejos de su estadio. Todo un reto para los de Pacheta, que han sabido adaptarse y sobreponerse a las dificultades para rendir en la carretera, donde ha logrado dos victorias consecutivas, rompiendo una racha de cuatro jornadas sin ganar que había despertado fantasmas del pasado. En el momento más crítico, los andaluces remontaron un 2-0 adverso para terminar llevándose los tres puntos en Zubieta. Y también ganaron en El Plantío, escenario donde ningún visitante había vencido hasta el momento. Dos resultados que colocan a los nazaríes como el tercer mejor equipo de la categoría como visitante (10 puntos), sólo por detrás de los registros de Eibar y Castellón (12). Para poner en valor lo que han logrado hasta la fecha los rojiblancos basta con comparar sus cifras actuales con las de la pasada campaña, en la que el Granada no logró su tercer triunfo a domicilio hasta la Jornada 23, ya en la segunda vuelta. Después de hacer los deberes cuando tocaba, ahora cambian las tornas: cuatro de los próximos cinco partidos serán en Los Cármenes, una circunstancia que puede catapultar a los nazaríes al siguiente nivel, aunque para ello tendrán que mejorar sus prestaciones como local. El Granada tiene ahora la misión de acercarse al pleno en estos próximos compromisos ante su afición, algo que permitiría a los rojiblancos asentarse en la zona alta de la tabla. Un privilegio del que no disfrutaron la temporada pasada y que ahora pueden alcanzar si son capaces de convertir Los Cármenes en un fortín.

Sports fans are accustomed to higher prices for concessions, but Los Angeles FC's recent promo night may have raised the bar.

The club celebrated "Hello Kitty Night" with Wednesday's 3-1 win over Austin FC, and speciality concession items accompanied the theme.

Two photos circulated on social media showing the Hello Kitty nachos and tacos went for $54.99 apiece. Based on a series of Reddit posts , that appeared to be the general price for any of the food items that came with the LAFC/Hello Kitty-branded lunchbox.

At least LAFC sent the supporters home with three points. Denis Bouanga scored the opener in the 52nd minute and quickly responded after Brandon Vázquez equalized in the 66th. Son Heung-Min provided some insurance with a 72nd-minute goal.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino apologises for World Cup sell-off plan, but told he’s ‘not fit to be Fifa president’
articles.summary: FA chair Debbie Hewitt received ‘no new information’ to change her position during the three-and-a-half hour meeting and said Infantino had still not answere...
articles.body:
Gianni Infantino has apologised to the Fifa Council for his World Cup sell-off plan but has been told he's still "not fit to be Fifa president" after failing to answer questions from his critics.

The FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who sits on the Fifa Council, told reporters in Zurich that Uefa's position in opposing Infantino has not changed after he attempted to sell stakes in the World Cup and Fifa tournaments to private investors this summer.

Hewitt also said that Infantino did not answer the Council's questions relating to other recent controversies, including his involvement in overturning Folarin Balogun 's suspension at the World Cup after a call from Donald Trump and the Fifa Peace Prize.

Hewitt said Infantino has requested members to submit their questions in writing, despite a three-and-a-half hour meeting of the Fifa Council in what was their first official gathering since details of the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan emerged in July.

"The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be Fifa president, and that was what was shared in the meeting," Hewitt told reporters in Zurich.

"He's told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it's up to him to do that, and do that in the open way. The minimum is having the papers from FFE [the Fifa Forward Enterprise plan], because if there's nothing to hide, then share them with us."

Infantino outlined his plans for form within Fifa last month and is planning to stand for re-election in March after coming under pressure to resign following the collapse of his World Cup sell-off plan.

A lengthy statement from Fifa after the meeting confirmed that Infantino had apologised "for the mistakes made in relation to the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal" and called for unity, while reiterating that "football is for everyone, everywhere".

Uefa led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

FA chair Hewitt also wrote to Infantino last month calling for an independent review into the World Cup private investor plan and the handling of the Balogun case.

The decision to pause Balogun's suspension came before US president Donald Trump admitted he personally contacted Infantino to request that the red card given to the forward against Bosnia and Herzegovina be re-examined.

Hewitt said Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for not sharing the FFE plan with them before details of it were reported by The Times in the week following the World Cup final and that she believed he "regrets that deeply".

But she added that she received "no new information" to change her position after the FA withdrew their support for Infantino following the loss of confidence in his leadership.

"We spoke a lot about the issues and it's fair to say Gianni apologised for what happened," Hewitt said. "He said that with some contrition and there were no holds barred on what we felt about what happened.

"We were asked to submit our questions and one of the disappointing things is we did not get the answers to those questions. We didn't get answers to anything we had specifically requested, for example getting the papers from FFE.

"I asked the question 'why and why not?' and we were asked to submit those questions and then we will get answers. To be fair, there were so many questions. Certainly I've left the room feeling there's nothing I wished I had said and didn't say.

"I have no new information that makes me feel any differently about how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of Fifa who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly, a promise again that we will get the information that we've requested."

articles.title: Un nuevo golpe complica el despegue de Gonzalo Petit
articles.standfirst: El delantero cedido por el Betis vuelve a ver interrumpida su adaptación por una lesión en el bíceps femoral
articles.summary: El delantero cedido por el Betis vuelve a ver interrumpida su adaptación por una lesión en el bíceps femoral
articles.body: Gonzalo Petit buscaba minutos en el Cádiz y, de momento, vuelve a encontrarse con la enfermería. El delantero uruguayo, propiedad del Real Betis, sufre una lesión muscular que añade otra dificultad a un inicio de temporada en el que apenas ha podido participar. El conjunto amarillo ha informado de que el atacante sintió molestias durante una acción del entrenamiento del lunes. Las pruebas posteriores confirmaron una "lesión muscular mioaponeurótica en el bíceps femoral" que le impedirá estar disponible este domingo contra el Granada y, seguramente, tampoco estará en los próximos compromisos. No hay un plazo de recuperación establecido. El club deja su regreso pendiente de evolución. La realidad es que Petit llegó cedido durante el mercado de verano para reforzar el ataque, pero un problema físico ya retrasó su incorporación a la competición. Después tampoco consiguió hacerse un sitio y su pobre balance se limita a ocho minutos ante la UD Las Palmas. El Betis había apostado por el uruguayo después de que destacara muy joven en el fútbol de su país. La pasada temporada comenzó cedido en el Mirandés y cambió de destino en enero para incorporarse al Granada. El Cádiz representaba una nueva oportunidad de acumular experiencia y continuidad, pero el comienzo está siendo complicado y desde el club verdiblanco ya están replanteándose qué hacer con una joven promesa que no arranca en Europa. La competencia también pesa. Vladys es actualmente la referencia ofensiva del Cádiz, que cuenta además con Izeta y Álvaro García entre sus opciones para la delantera. En ese escenario, Petit necesita continuidad para convencer a Celades, y la nueva lesión le resta entrenamientos y otra convocatoria en un momento en el que todavía busca su espacio. De momento, su siguiente paso es recuperarse.

articles.title: Martin Ho: Tottenham Women boss on summer signings, WSL start and facing Chelsea and Arsenal
articles.summary: Watch Chelsea vs Tottenham in the WSL live on Sky Sports Football and Sky Sports Mix from 11.30am on Sunday; kick-off 12pm; watch free in-game clips and match highlights shortly after full-time on Sky Sports' digital platforms
articles.body:
Spurs started the 2026/27 season with statement wins against Crystal Palace and Aston Villa, winning by an aggregate of 11-0 - but they came crashing back down to earth with a 6-1 defeat to London City Lionesses before the international break.

It would have offered Tottenham boss Martin Ho and his players a sharp reminder about the task they have on their hands if they want to finish in the Champions League spots this season - and it does not get any easier with Chelsea and Arsenal to come in the next two games, starting at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

But the ever-pragmatic Ho will not have forgotten that. Spurs have gone from relegation contenders to European consideration in less than 18 months under the former Brann boss, but any route to the top will not be straight forward.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports , he said: "You're always optimistic that it can go well, but I'm also realistic that you don't just have this long-term success. It's not linear, there's going to be ups and downs, but I know if you want long-term consistency, you're going to have to have this.

"We can't just go from being a team that's been fighting at the bottom of the table to go and challenge for the [WSL] trophy and make that successful and consistent over years to come. There's a process to that but the ambition is always to be at the top of that table.

"Since coming in, I've tried to push standards, push the expectation with staff and players to give us a platform that can give us an opportunity to progress.

"The players deserve a lot of credit for that because they take the information and run with it. They play with courage, bravery, with personality which is what I asked for and their commitment and willingness is first class.

"Maybe there were times early on when I thought it was going to take a lot longer to get to where we want to be identity-wise, but the players deserve the credit because they've enabled us to maybe accelerate a little bit quicker than what I probably thought."

Part of that has come through shrewd recruitment, particularly this summer. Spurs signed Champions League winners Victoria Pelova and Alice Sombath from Arsenal and Lyon respectively, Caitlin Dijkstra also joined from Wolfsburg in just a few of the impressive incomings.

It all follows Ho's plan of bringing in different experiences from league, European and international levels to strengthen the squad and add a steel they were perhaps missing in his first year.

"We felt like we needed certain qualities in certain positions and those players that have come in have allowed us to do that," Ho said.

"They've also been in environments where they've been competing in different ways, they'll bring those experiences here which was important for us that we have a diverse environment and culture.

"You also want to make sure you get a balance also between the youth and experience of the squad. You want to get a balance of where you feel relationships can be built and where they can be long-term on the pitch.

"Alice [Sombath] was one of those in that position where she's had such wonderful experiences at Lyon of winning titles, but also internationally, she's got really good credibility at such a young age. The opportunity to bring her in was huge for us and someone we have followed for a while.

"Then people like Victoria [Pelova], who's coming off the back of a long-term injury. She was maybe low of confidence and wasn't in a place where she felt her football could go forward. The opportunity to bring her here after having those conversations was important.

"She's been part of a winning culture and a winning environment and those environments are what we want to bring to the club, which she can share and we can lean on those experiences from her.

"But since she's come in, she's been outstanding in terms of giving her the enthusiasm again to play football, but giving her the confidence and belief she can achieve what she wants in terms of own ambitions."

On October 24, Pelova will be reunited with her former Arsenal team-mates in the north London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. It is the site of Spurs' only win against the Gunners in any competition, and given their rivals' own dismal start to the season, might be sensing another.

Before that though, a resurgent Chelsea - and another insight into whether this Tottenham team have what it takes to compete against the WSL's best.

"You have to show a willingness to compete in those games first," Ho reflected. "You go in with the mindset and the objective is always to win the game, but we have to look at the process behind that first and the performance has to allow you to be in that position psychologically.

"Are they going to be tough games? 100 percent, but they're the games you want to play and I want to play in as a coach, the players want to play in. The commercial interest is big in those because they're London derbies so you have to embrace them as a player.

"But they're the ones where you will really see the character and belief of the group, they're the ones where you'll really see the development and the progress of the team, but one game doesn't tell you if you're a good team or a bad team.

"It maybe gives you some answers in terms of where we need to go and the direction we need to go in, but it doesn't define you."

After a bruising defeat nearly two weeks ago, Spurs will have a point to prove in their next two games. While they might not define them as a team, it could go some way in defining where they finish come May.

articles.title: Demichelis: 'Bayern shaped me as a player, a coach and a person'
articles.summary: Martín Demichelis joined FC Bayern from River Plate in 2003 and went on to become an immensely important defender in Munich. While with the record champions,...
articles.body:
Martín Demichelis joined FC Bayern from River Plate in 2003 and went on to become an immensely important defender in Munich. While with the record champions, his coaches included Ottmar Hitzfeld, Felix Magath and Louis van Gaal; he won four doubles and narrowly missed out on the treble in the 2010 Champions League final. In 2019, he began his coaching career at the FCB U19s, before going on to lead the FC Bayern reserves. In 2022, he returned to River Plate as head coach and won the Argentine league title at the first time of asking. Since the start of the season, "Micho" has been in the dugout at RB Leipzig – who face FC Bayern in the Bundesliga's standout fixture at 18:30 CET at the Allianz Arena on Saturday evening.

Micho, you're returning to the Allianz Arena for a competitive match for the first time – what will you be feeling when you take your place in the RB Leipzig dugout as coach? "I lived in Munich for many years and represented FC Bayern both as a player and a coach. Returning to the Allianz Arena now with RB Leipzig is something special for me. I'm looking forward to seeing some familiar faces again, and above all to the match itself. Because, whilst I have the utmost respect for FC Bayern, I naturally want RB Leipzig to come out on top on Saturday."

When you left Munich, you described FC Bayern as your 'second home'. How special is it to play against a club that had such a profound influence on you? "I'll never forget the trust that FC Bayern placed in me back then when they signed me in 2003. FC Bayern shaped me over a total of 12 years as a player and later as a coach – and as a person too. It was always my dream to be a coach in the Bundesliga. I'm very proud that I'm now able to fulfil this dream at a top club like RB Leipzig."

After a difficult start to the season, you've recently thrashed Frankfurt and beaten PSV with Leipzig. What has changed within the team – and how sustainable is this resurgence? "We spoke openly and used specific examples to show what had worked well and what we needed to change. Everyone understood what we were getting at. We want to build on that, continue to develop and keep on being successful – in the Bundesliga, the Champions League and the DFB Cup."

You've played for FC Bayern in Munich and are famiiar with the special atmosphere of the stadium and the Bayern fans. What will your players need to do on Saturday to have a chance there? "We must remain true to our own principles. From the first matchday to the last, we want to embody what sets RB Leipzig apart – including thi Saturday. That means we'll try to deliver the best possible performance using the methods we believe to be the best."

articles.title: Cashman Field prepares for historic farewell
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (KLAS) — After decades of memories, Cashman Field is coming down and this morning Good Day Las Vegas’ JC Fernandez was live inside the historic sta...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (KLAS) -- After decades of memories, Cashman Field is coming down and this morning Good Day Las Vegas' JC Fernandez was live inside the historic stadium looking back at its past and previewing Saturday's Las Vegas Lights FC match, the final event ever at Cashman Field before the site makes way for redevelopment.

JC was joined by Will Martin, the Lights' director of marketing and communications, who talked about Cashman's history, which dates back to 1947, when the original stadium was built as Elks Stadium. The modern Cashman Field opened on April 1, 1983, with a Major League Baseball exhibition between the San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners.

The stadium became home to the minor league baseball team, the Las Vegas Stars, who played there from 1983 through 2000, followed by the Las Vegas 51s, from 2001 through 2018, and eventually the Las Vegas Aviators. The Lights arrived in 2018, adding professional soccer to Cashman's long sporting history.

The venue also has a Raiders connection. Long before the team called Las Vegas home, the Oakland Raiders faced the Houston Oilers at the original Cashman Field in a 1964 American Football League preseason game. Oakland won 34-20.

Martin also recalled a May 1955 boxing match between Archie Moore and Nino Valdes, with Moore winning a 15-round decision. Baseball brought its own milestone in 1993, when a Chicago White Sox–Chicago Cubs exhibition drew more than 15,000 fans, setting Cashman's attendance record.

Beyond sports, JC highlighted Cashman's concert history, including appearances by the Beach Boys, Ice Cube and Metallica. While Metallica fans can now catch the band at Sphere, JC noted that tickets for its September 1998 Cashman show started at just $30.

The focus then shifted to Cashman's final night. Las Vegas Lights FC will host Lexington SC on Saturday, October 17, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. Martin showcased a miniature replica of the stadium that will be given away to early arriving fans while supplies last.

Plus, fans will see fireworks before the match and a light show afterward. With a sellout expected, Martin encouraged fans to purchase tickets in advance.

articles.title: La defensa es sólo la mitad del problema
articles.standfirst: Etxeberria y Neva señalan la fragilidad atrás como principal asignatura, pero el Alba es también el equipo menos goleador de la categoría
articles.summary: Etxeberria y Neva señalan la fragilidad atrás como principal asignatura, pero el Alba es también el equipo menos goleador de la categoría
articles.body: Dos ruedas de prensa en dos días y un mismo diagnóstico. Carlos Neva, uno de los capitanes del Alba, aseguró ayer miércoles que "todo el mundo es consciente de que tenemos que empezar a construir desde atrás, desde la solidez defensiva", y Joseba Etxeberria ha hecho suyo ese análisis este jueves al señalar que "el principal problema que tenemos es la forma de defender". Los números respaldan a ambos: el Alba ha encajado 20 goles en nueve jornadas, los mismos que Ceuta y Córdoba (la cifra más alta de la categoría), y su balance de 5 goles a favor y 20 en contra es el peor de toda la Liga. A estas alturas del curso pasado, el equipo había dejado la portería a cero en cuatro ocasiones; este año todavía no lo ha conseguido. Donde ambos difieren es en el reparto de la responsabilidad. Neva, que definió lo ocurrido en Valladolid como un "accidente gordísimo", sostuvo que "la máxima responsabilidad de que estemos ahí abajo es de los 25 jugadores que estamos ahí dentro" y apartó del problema a un técnico que llevaba una semana en el cargo. Etxeberria, preguntado por esas palabras, no las comparte ("no estoy de acuerdo") y asume su responsabilidad: "Es también culpa mía por el plan de partido defensivo". Lo argumenta remarcando que defender es cosa de todos y que la solución empieza también por los jugadores de arriba, a quienes pide que aprieten y ensucien las jugadas del rival para que todo sea más fácil para los de atrás. Pero la defensa es sólo la mitad de la ecuación. El Alba ha marcado 5 goles en nueve jornadas y es el equipo menos goleador de toda la competición: nueve menos que los 14 que llevaba a estas alturas de la pasada temporada, mientras que ha encajado cuatro más (20 frente a 16). Etxeberria sitúa el foco en la fase defensiva, y el ataque aparece de pasada en su análisis: "Mejorar en esa fase (la defensiva) sobre todo, también en la fase ofensiva". En ese contexto, el conjunto manchego visita el sábado El Molinón, donde la temporada pasada demostró que, aunque las cosas vayan mal, todo puede suceder si no se bajan los brazos: el equipo remontó un 3-0 y se llevó el partido (3-4) en un final épico. Pero eso es pasado y, centrados en el presente, Etxeberria rechaza que el partido sea una final: "Calificarlo así puede ser excesivo con todo lo que queda", aunque sí se compromete con el cambio: "Estoy convencido de que ya desde este fin de semana las cosas van a cambiar". Un cambio que, con los números en la mano, pasa por defender mucho mejor, pero también por empezar a marcar goles.

articles.title: FIFA revisará el caso Balogun y el Premio de la Paz
articles.standfirst: El máximo organismo del fútbol mundial se compromete tras el Consejo celebrado en Zúrich a analizar de cara al futuro ambos casos, no exentos de una enorme polémica
articles.summary: El máximo organismo del fútbol mundial se compromete tras el Consejo celebrado en Zúrich a analizar de cara al futuro ambos casos, no exentos de una enorme polémica
articles.body: El Consejo de la FIFA celebrado hoy en Zúrich no solo ha servido para plasmar la división del fútbol mundial pese a los esfuerzos de Gianni Infantino de pedir unidad y disculpas a su vez a las confederaciones por los errores cometidos en cuanto a la forma en que se llevó a cabo y se comunicó el proyecto FFE, del que insistió que se había retirado definitivamente y no volvería a aparecer de ninguna forma. Pero la FIFA se ha comprometido también de cara al futuro a revisar los procesos disciplinarios tras el polémico caso Balogún y el Premio de la Paz, que también dio que hablar al ser Donald Trump el primer elegido antes del Mundial de Estados Unidos y tras las quejas formales presentadas por miembros del Consejo (como Bernd Neuendorf, presidente de la Federación Alemana). "El Consejo de la FIFA acordó establecer un grupo de trabajo que incluirá a miembros de todas las confederaciones para examinar en detalle el marco de gobernanza de la FIFA, mientras que el Comité de Responsabilidad Social del Fútbol de la FIFA recibió el encargo de evaluar el Premio de la Paz de la FIFA, cuya decisión se tomará en la próxima reunión del Consejo en diciembre de 2026", apunta FIFA en su nota de prensa. "Tras la decisión adoptada por el Comité Disciplinario independiente de la FIFA de suspender durante un período de prueba de un año la sanción de un partido impuesta a Folarin Balogun, de Estados Unidos, tras su expulsión contra Bosnia y Herzegovina en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2026, se acordó que el Comité Jurídico de la FIFA llevará a cabo una revisión de los procedimientos disciplinarios de la FIFA y que también se realizará una presentación en la próxima reunión del Consejo de la FIFA en diciembre de 2026", añadió. La prioridad de las voces más críticas por el escándalo Balogun era modificar de urgencia el Artículo 27 del Código Disciplinario para que se impida suspender o aplazar las sanciones automáticas de un partido provocadas por una tarjeta roja directa. De este modo, la FIFA cerraría el vacío legal para evitar que se repita un caso como el del último Mundial y que destapó el propio Trump, que desveló que llamó a Infatino para que estudiara quitar la tarjeta roja al jugador de su país. La administración de la FIFA presentó al Consejo de la FIFA una propuesta denominada Programa de Solidaridad de Superávits de la FIFA, que utilizaría una parte de las reservas de la FIFA para duplicar con creces el nivel de financiación previsto para el período 2027-2030, hasta alcanzar los 6.350 millones de dólares. “Como se ha dicho en numerosas ocasiones desde 2016, el dinero de la FIFA, incluidas sus reservas, pertenece a las 211 federaciones miembro de la FIFA, y la propuesta de aumentar la inversión en todas las federaciones miembro de la FIFA, confederaciones y demás partes interesadas hasta alcanzar los 6.350 millones de dólares tiene como objetivo reforzar nuestro firme compromiso de seguir apoyando el desarrollo y el acceso al fútbol a nivel mundial gracias al excelente resultado financiero de la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2026”, declaró Infantino.
